college_identity.identity_notes: One of India's oldest engineering institutions, tracing origin to an 1886 survey training school; became Bihar College of Engineering in 1924; upgraded to NIT status in 2004 (to replace Bihar's lost REC, which had been in Jamshedpur before Jharkhand's formation); declared Institute of National Importance in 2007. Currently operates across TWO campuses: an older, smaller main campus (~34-40 acres) on Ashok Rajpath Road in Patna city, and a newer, larger Bihta campus (~120-165 acres, figures vary by source) still under construction, to which some branches (reportedly CSE and ECE for certain years) have begun relocating. Explicitly verified DISTINCT from IIT Patna (a separate, newer institution in Bihta) and BIT Mesra – Patna Campus (also separate) — no evidence from either was included in this extraction.

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'Placements at NIT Patna are good for CSE. The students become eligible from 7th semester. Average package is around 13 to 14 LPA. Highest goes to 40. Around 85 to 95 percent students get placed.'
'Girls to boys ratio is low, around 1 ratio 5 or 1 ratio 6.'
'Faculty teaching quality is mixed. Some are good and some are average.'
'Infrastructure is average, like for Patna campus; however Bihta campus is under construction.' Descriptive of the two-campus situation.

review_items.extraction_note: This review explicitly frames the branch-based campus assignment (some branches at the older, smaller Patna campus vs. others at the newer, larger Bihta campus) as a form of perceived unfairness — a genuinely distinctive and specific concern for this institution given its unusual two-campus transition.
